mainTopic: The limits of יום הכפורים's atonement: known sins, מלקות, doubtful cases of טומאה, and sins discovered after יום הכפורים
overview: The גמרא gives a simple source for why a known sinner still brings his חטאת after יום הכפורים: יום הכפורים atones only for a sin that only the מקום knows about. רבא then rules that someone who owes מלקות is still lashed after יום הכפורים. A משנה seems to say otherwise, and the גמרא answers that the משנה speaks of someone who was not warned. Next the גמרא tests the principle on a series of doubtful cases: the יולדת, the מצורע, the נזיר, the סוטה and the עגלה ערופה. Each time it explains why יום הכפורים does not exempt them. Some קרבנות come for טומאה or to permit eating קדשים, not for atonement. In other cases someone does know about the sin, or a פסוק demands a special atonement. Finally, the גמרא asks why a person who finds out about his sin after יום הכפורים must still bring a חטאת. After a long back-and-forth about the word 'knowing' written for the יחיד, the נשיא and the צבור, it learns this from the extra word by the נשיא. אביי then begins to challenge that proof, and his argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A simpler source: יום הכפורים atones only for sins only ה׳ knows about
steps.stepSummary: Instead of the verses used by רב דימי and אביי, the גמרא proves the rule from the teaching that יום הכפורים atones only for a sin only the מקום knows of. A sin the person knows about is not atoned, so he still owes his קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: To prove this rule, we don't need רב דימי's source or אביי's source. Instead, take this teaching: for a sin that only the מקום knows about, יום הכפורים atones. That means only such a sin is atoned by יום הכפורים, but a sin the person knows he did is not atoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside the earlier proofs of רב דימי and אביי and offers a different, simpler source for why a person still brings his חטאת or definite אשם after יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source says יום הכפורים atones for a sin 'that only the מקום knows of', meaning a sin the person is unsure about. From that wording we learn the flip side: a sin the person knows for sure he did is not covered by יום הכפורים. So someone who owes a חטאת or a definite אשם still has to bring it afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: to resolve it, to find a clear source for it
is aware of it, knows about it

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רב דימי and אביי are wrong. It is only showing that their verses are not needed, because a simpler source already proves the rule.

phrases.english: To resolve it, not from the teaching of רב דימי
and not from that of אביי,
rather, from this:
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier teaching on the verse 'מכל חטאתיכם לפני ה' תטהרו' (ויקרא 16:30).

phrases.aramaic: חֵטְא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמָּקוֹם –
phrases.english: a sin that no one is aware of except the Omnipresent —
Yom Kippur atones.
And from it we learn:

phrases.aramaic: חֵטְא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמָּקוֹם
phrases.english: it is a sin that no one is aware of except the Omnipresent
that Yom Kippur atones for,
but one that he knows about — it does not atone.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִפְשְׁטַהּ לָא מִדְּרַב דִּימִי וְלָא מִדְּאַבַּיֵּי, אֶלָּא מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source for the rule that רב דימי and אביי had derived from verses earlier on the דף.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that those who owe a חטאת or a definite אשם must still bring it after יום הכפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that יום הכפורים atones only for a sin that only the מקום knows of, which implies a known sin is not atoned.
steps.whatToRemember: יום הכפורים atones for sins a person does not know about. A sin he knows about still needs its own קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that יום הכפורים's atonement has limits: it does not cancel a known obligation to bring a קרבן.

steps.title: Someone who owes מלקות still gets them after יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא, father of רב הונא, quotes רבא: a person who became liable for מלקות remains liable even after יום הכפורים has passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא, the father of רב הונא, said in the name of רבא: people who are liable for lashes, and יום הכפורים passed over them, are still liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is given: יום הכפורים does not cancel a punishment of מלקות that a person already owes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new case to the topic. Just as יום הכפורים does not cancel a known person's קרבן, it also does not cancel the lashes he owes from בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: that passed over them (they lived through it)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: And רב תחליפא, the father of רב הונא, said
in the name of רבא:
Those liable to lashes
over whom Yom Kippur has passed are liable.
phrases.notes: He means they still receive their lashes after יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the idea that יום הכפורים does not cancel known obligations from קרבנות to מלקות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone liable for מלקות is still lashed after יום הכפורים passes.

steps.title: Why say this? It is the same as sin and guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא's ruling is needed, since we already know that someone who owes a חטאת or a definite אשם still brings it after יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! How is this any different from people who owe sin offerings and definite guilt offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know יום הכפורים does not cancel a known person's חטאת or definite אשם. So it seems it should also not cancel his מלקות, and רבא seems to be teaching nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: definite guilt offerings (brought for a sin the person knows he did)

phrases.english: It's obvious!
How is it different from those liable to sin offerings
and definite guilt offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! מַאי שְׁנָא מֵחַיָּיבֵי חַטָּאוֹת וַאֲשָׁמוֹת וַדָּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's ruling in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that מלקות are still given after יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It already follows from the known rule about חטאות and definite אשמות, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought bodily punishment is different from a money obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a קרבן is a monetary obligation, while מלקות is a bodily punishment. We might have thought יום הכפורים cancels a bodily punishment, so רבא teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: there, with the offerings, it is a money matter. But here, where it is about the body, say no, he is not lashed. So רבא teaches us that he is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing there was a real reason to think מלקות might be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן costs money, and יום הכפורים does not erase money one owes. Lashes are a punishment on the person's body, so one might think יום הכפורים, which atones for the person, would cancel them. רבא teaches that it does not; he is still lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have thought to say
he teaches us (that it is not so)

phrases.english: You might have thought to say:
there, it is a monetary matter,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the חטאות and definite אשמות, which cost money to bring.

phrases.english: but here, where it is bodily,
say no, he is not lashed,
so he teaches us that he is.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by explaining why רבא's ruling was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a reasonable mistaken assumption (סלקא דעתך) that the ruling comes to block.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מלקות is a bodily punishment and not a monetary obligation, יום הכפורים might cancel it.
steps.terutzMaskana: יום הכפורים does not cancel מלקות; the person is still lashed afterward.
steps.whatToRemember: יום הכפורים does not cancel a known person's קרבן (a money matter) or his מלקות (a bodily punishment). רבא had to say the second because bodily punishment might have seemed different.

steps.title: A משנה seems to say יום הכפורים atones even for prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a משנה that says יום הכפורים atones for every kind of sin, even a לא תעשה that normally carries מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: whether he became aware or did not become aware, whether it is a positive מצוה or a prohibition, יום הכפורים atones for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling from Step 2. It quotes a משנה that seems to say יום הכפורים atones even for prohibitions, which usually carry מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most prohibitions in the תורה carry מלקות. If the משנה says יום הכפורים atones for a לא תעשה, it sounds like יום הכפורים wipes out the מלקות too. That directly contradicts רבא, who said the person stays liable for מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether he found out about the sin before יום הכפורים or did not find out
A positive מצוה, a command to do something
A prohibition. Most prohibitions carry מלקות.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שבועות 2b, which talks about what יום הכפורים atones for.

phrases.english: whether he became aware or did not become aware,
whether a positive מצוה or a prohibition!
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה, which the גמרא assumes here, says that יום הכפורים atones for all of these.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 4 explained why רבא's ruling was needed, the גמרא now challenges whether the ruling is even true.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that someone liable for מלקות stays liable after יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says יום הכפורים atones for prohibitions. Prohibitions carry מלקות, so it sounds like יום הכפורים removes the מלקות.

steps.title: Warned versus not warned
steps.stepSummary: רבא is talking about someone who was warned before sinning, so he is liable for מלקות. The משנה is talking about someone who was not warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling of רבא is about a case where they warned him. That משנה is about a case where they did not warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the cases. רבא and the משנה are not talking about the same situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית דין can give מלקות only if witnesses warned the sinner (התראה) right before he sinned. If he was warned, he is truly liable for מלקות, and יום הכפורים does not remove it. That is רבא's case. If he was not warned, there is no מלקות to begin with, and יום הכפורים gives full atonement. That is the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase opens an answer that resolves a contradiction.
They warned him before he sinned
A warning given by witnesses. It is required before בית דין can give מלקות.

steps.whatToRemember: יום הכפורים atones for a prohibition. But if the sinner was warned and became liable for מלקות, יום הכפורים does not cancel the מלקות.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where they warned him,
phrases.notes: "This" means רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: that is where they did not warn him.
phrases.notes: "That" means the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 5 by putting רבא and the משנה in different cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בכך, הא בכך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say יום הכפורים cancels the מלקות for every prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a sinner who was not warned gets full atonement. A sinner who was warned stays liable for מלקות.

steps.title: Challenge from a woman unsure if she owes a birth offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid for a series of challenges. Then it asks the first one: a ספק יולדת should be exempt after יום הכפורים, since only the מקום knows whether she owes a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so (memory aid: a יולדת, a מצורע, a נזיר, a סוטה, in a heifer), a woman unsure whether she gave birth, who had יום הכפורים pass, should not bring her קרבן. יום הכפורים already atoned for her, because this is a sin that only the מקום knows about!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the principle from Step 1, that יום הכפורים atones for a sin only the מקום knows of. It starts a series of challenges against it, listed in a memory aid, and asks the first one here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who miscarried and does not know whether it counts as a birth is unsure if she owes a חטאת. Only the מקום knows the truth, so this looks just like the case of an אשם תלוי. If יום הכפורים exempts the אשם תלוי, it should exempt her too. Yet she still brings her קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so. This phrase opens a challenge showing that a principle leads to an unacceptable result.
A memory aid listing the topics the גמרא will discuss next
A woman who is unsure whether what she miscarried counts as a birth that obligates a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not against רבא. It goes back to the earlier principle that יום הכפורים atones for a sin only the מקום knows of.

phrases.english: But if that is so,
(A memory aid: a woman who gave birth, a leper,
a nazirite, a sotah, in a heifer),

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק יוֹלֶדֶת שֶׁעָבַר עָלֶיהָ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
phrases.english: a woman uncertain whether she gave birth, over whom Yom Kippur passed,
should not bring her offering,
since Yom Kippur atoned for her,
for it is a sin that no one knows of
except the Omnipresent!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the topic of רבא and מלקות, the גמרא returns to the principle from Step 1 and begins testing it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that יום הכפורים atones for a sin only the מקום knows of, which exempts an uncertain sinner from his קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ספק יולדת's obligation is also known only to the מקום, so she should be exempt after יום הכפורים. But she is not.

steps.title: יום הכפורים atones for sins, not for impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא explains from a פסוק that יום הכפורים atones only for sins. The יולדת's קרבן is not for a sin; it is part of her purification from טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: The פסוק says "for all their sins," and not for all their impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא answers the challenge. The ספק יולדת is different because her קרבן has nothing to do with a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that יום הכפורים exempts an uncertain sinner only works where the קרבן comes to atone for a sin. The פסוק limits יום הכפורים to "their sins." A יולדת brings her חטאת to finish becoming טהור so she may eat קדשים, not to atone. So יום הכפורים does not replace her קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: For all their sins. The פסוק describing what יום הכפורים atones for.
Ritual purity. The יולדת's קרבן is part of her purification.

steps.whatToRemember: יום הכפורים covers sins only. A קרבן that comes for טומאה or purification, like the יולדת's, is still brought after יום הכפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary of the earlier principle. יום הכפורים can stand in for a קרבן only when that קרבן comes to atone for a sin.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
"For all their sins" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:21

phrases.english: and not for all their impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: לְכׇל חַטֹּאתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ספק יולדת raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on a פסוק: sin versus impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ספק יולדת's uncertain obligation looked like the אשם תלוי, so יום הכפורים should exempt her.
steps.terutzMaskana: יום הכפורים atones only for sins. Her קרבן is for טומאה and purification, so she still brings it.

steps.title: What about the view that a יולדת is a sinner?
steps.stepSummary: The answer of רב הושעיא works only if the יולדת's קרבן is not for a sin. But רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds that a יולדת is a sinner, so how does that answer work for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who says a woman who gave birth is a sinner, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 8. According to one תנא, the יולדת's קרבן does come because of a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said יום הכפורים does not cover the יולדת because her קרבן is about טומאה, not sin. רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds that she is a חוטאת. If so, her קרבן seems to be for a sin, and יום הכפורים should exempt her when she is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (how would he answer?)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai,
who says a woman who gave birth is a sinner,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי, דְּאָמַר יוֹלֶדֶת חוֹטֵאת הִיא, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 8 using another תנא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הושעיא's answer that the יולדת's קרבן is not for sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds that a יולדת is a sinner. So her קרבן should count as one brought for sin and be cleared by יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Her קרבן lets her eat קדשים; it is not for atonement
steps.stepSummary: Even according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, the יולדת's קרבן is brought to permit her to eat קדשים, not to bring כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a יולדת brings a קרבן, it is to become permitted to eat קדשים. She does not bring it for atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the purpose of the יולדת's קרבן is what matters. Its job is to permit her to eat קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if she had some sin, the קרבן is not what atones for it. Its function is the last stage of her purification, so that she may eat קדשים. Since יום הכפורים gives כפרה but not purification, she still has to bring it.

phrases.english: When a woman who gave birth brings an offering,
it is to become permitted to eat sacrificial food,
and she does not bring it for atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹלֶדֶת כִּי קָא מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן לְאִישְׁתְּרוֹיֵי בַּאֲכִילַת קָדָשִׁים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי שמעון בן יוחי calls her a sinner, her קרבן must be for כפרה, and יום הכפורים would exempt her.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her קרבן serves to permit her to eat קדשים. יום הכפורים does not do that, so she must still bring it.

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points to the משנה. It says a woman with a doubtful bird חטאת must bring it after יום הכפורים, because it makes her fit to eat זבחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this in the משנה. A woman who owes a doubtful bird חטאת, and יום הכפורים passed, must bring it after יום הכפורים, because it makes her fit to eat offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that the answer just given is already stated in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the very reason the גמרא just gave: her קרבן makes her fit to eat קדשים. So the idea is not a new invention. It is the משנה's own explanation of why יום הכפורים does not exempt her.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We too have learned this:
phrases.notes: He is quoting the משנה earlier in this פרק (25a).

phrases.english: A woman upon whom there is
a doubtful bird sin offering,
and Yom Kippur passed over her,
must bring it after Yom Kippur,
because it makes her fit to eat offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 10 from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that the יולדת's קרבן is brought to permit eating קדשים, not for כפרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 25a: 'מפני שמכשרתה לאכול בזבחים'.

steps.title: Then a ספק מצורע should not bring his קרבן
steps.stepSummary: If יום הכפורים clears doubtful sins, then a ספק מצורע should be exempt after יום הכפורים, since only the מקום knows the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a ספק מצורע for whom יום הכפורים passed should not bring his קרבן. יום הכפורים passed over him, and this is a sin that only the מקום knows about!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the next challenge in the series, this time about a person who may or may not be a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that יום הכפורים clears a sin known only to ה׳. A ספק מצורע is a doubtful case like that. So it would seem that after יום הכפורים he no longer needs to bring his קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so (introduces a challenge from the logic just stated)
Someone who is not sure if he is a מצורע

phrases.english: But if that is so,
an uncertain leper for whom Yom Kippur passed
should not bring his offering,
since Yom Kippur has passed over him,
for it is a sin that no one knows of
except the Omnipresent!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, סְפֵק מְצוֹרָע שֶׁעָבַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לָא מַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יולדת to a new case in the series of challenges.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that יום הכפורים clears doubtful obligations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ספק מצורע is a doubt known only to ה׳. So יום הכפורים should exempt him, yet in fact he brings his קרבן.

steps.title: Sins, not טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא answers from the פסוק 'לכל חטאתם': יום הכפורים atones for sins, not for impurities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: The פסוק says 'for all their sins', and not for all their impurities.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא gives the same answer he gave for the יולדת. The מצורע's קרבן is about טומאה, and יום הכפורים does not cover טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק limits the כפרה of יום הכפורים to חטאים. A מצורע's קרבן is part of his purification from טומאה. So even when he is in doubt, יום הכפורים does not exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: For all their sins (the פסוק about יום הכפורים)

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
"For all their sins"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:21

phrases.english: and not for all their impurities.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: לְכׇל חַטֹּאתָם וְלֹא לְכׇל טוּמְאֹתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 with the same פסוק used in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule using a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים clears any doubtful obligation, including a ספק מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: יום הכפורים atones only for sins. A מצורע's קרבן deals with טומאה, so he must still bring it.

steps.title: But צרעת comes because of sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי יוחנן said that נגעים come because of seven sins. So the מצורע's קרבן seems connected to sin after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: נגעים come because of seven things! (A memory aid: גג״ג ששל״ץ.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's answer. It shows that צרעת itself is caused by sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא treated the מצורע's קרבן as purely about טומאה. But if צרעת comes from seven sins, the קרבן looks like it is for sin. Then יום הכפורים should cover it after all.
steps.confusionAlert: The letters גג״ג ששל״ץ are not words. Each letter is the first letter of one of the seven sins that bring צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Leprous marks come because of seven things!
(A memory aid: gimmel gimmel gimmel, shin shin lamed tzadi)
phrases.notes: The letters stand for גילוי עריות, גסות הרוח, גזל, שפיכות דמים, שבועת שוא, לשון הרע, and צרות העין.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's claim that the מצורע's קרבן is about טומאה, not sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צרעת is caused by sins, so the מצורע's קרבן should count as a קרבן for sin, and יום הכפורים should clear it.

steps.title: The מצורע's קרבן lets him eat קדשים
steps.stepSummary: Even though צרעת comes from sin, the מצורע's קרבן is not for כפרה. It is brought to permit him to eat קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a מצורע brings his קרבן, he does not bring it for atonement. It is to become permitted to eat קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in the same way it answered for the יולדת in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin may have caused the צרעת, but the קרבן's job is not to atone for that sin. Its job is to finish his purification so he can eat קדשים. Since יום הכפורים does not do this, he still brings the קרבן after יום הכפורים.
steps.whatToRemember: יום הכפורים exempts doubtful obligations only when the קרבן is for כפרה. The קרבנות of the יולדת and the מצורע are brought to permit eating קדשים, so they must still be brought after יום הכפורים, even if a sin was involved.

phrases.english: When a leper brings his offering,
he does not bring it for atonement,
rather, it is to become permitted to eat sacrificial food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצוֹרָע כִּי מַיְיתֵי לָאו לְכַפָּרָה מַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 using the same idea as Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since צרעת comes from sin, the מצורע's קרבן is for כפרה, and יום הכפורים would exempt him.
steps.terutzMaskana: His קרבן serves to permit him to eat קדשים, not to atone. So יום הכפורים does not exempt him.

steps.title: What about a ספק נזיר after יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a ספק נזיר who may have become טמא should be exempt from his קרבן after יום הכפורים, since only the מקום knows the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, an uncertain נזיר who had יום הכפורים pass over him should not bring an offering, because יום הכפורים already atoned. This is a sin that only the מקום knows about!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the same idea from the earlier steps onto a new case: a נזיר who is not sure if he became טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea being tested is that יום הכפורים clears a doubtful sin that only the מקום knows about. A ספק נזיר also has a doubt that only the מקום knows. So it seems he too should be exempt from his קרבן after יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so (introduces a challenge based on what was just said)
A נזיר who is not sure if he became impure
The Omnipresent, a name for ה׳

phrases.english: But if that is so,

phrases.aramaic: סְפֵק נָזִיר שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
phrases.english: an uncertain nazir for whom Yom Kippur has passed
should not bring an offering,
since Yom Kippur already atoned,

phrases.aramaic: דְּחֵטְא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמָּקוֹם הוּא!
phrases.english: for it is a sin that only the Omnipresent knows about!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, סְפֵק נָזִיר שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same challenge from the מצורע to a new case, the ספק נזיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that יום הכפורים atones for a doubtful sin known only to the מקום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ספק נזיר's doubt is also known only to the מקום, so the rule would wrongly exempt him from his קרבן.

steps.title: יום הכפורים atones for sins, not טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא repeats his answer: the פסוק says 'for all their sins', not for all their impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: 'For all their sins', and not for all their impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers the challenge with the same פסוק he used for the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר's קרבן here is about טומאה, not about a sin. יום הכפורים atones only for sins, so it does not remove the doubtful נזיר's obligation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
"For all sin" – and not for all impurity.
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק he used in step 13, 'לכל חטאתם'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 the same way step 13 answered step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ספק נזיר is exempt because יום הכפורים cleared his doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: His קרבן comes for טומאה, which יום הכפורים does not cover, so he must still bring it.

steps.title: But one view calls the נזיר a sinner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי אלעזר הקפר, a נזיר is a sinner, so his קרבן seems to be about sin after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אלעזר הקפר, who says a נזיר is a sinner, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אושעיא's answer. One opinion holds that the נזיר is connected to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא's answer depends on the נזיר's קרבן being about טומאה only. If a נזיר counts as a חוטא, his קרבן looks like it is for sin. Then יום הכפורים should cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (asking how an answer works for this opinion)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Elazar ben HaKappar,
who says: a nazir is a sinner,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן הַקַּפָּר, דְּאָמַר: נָזִיר חוֹטֵא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17, the same way step 14 challenged step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's claim that the נזיר's קרבן is about טומאה, not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a נזיר is a חוטא, his קרבן is tied to sin, and 'לכל חטאתם' would include it.

steps.title: The נזיר's offering permits him to eat קדשים
steps.stepSummary: Even if a נזיר is a sinner, his קרבן is not for כפרה. It permits him to eat קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a נזיר brings an offering, he does not bring it for atonement. It is to permit him to eat קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the purpose of the נזיר's קרבן is not atonement. This matches the answer given for the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being called a sinner does not make the קרבן a כפרה offering. The קרבן's job is to let him eat קדשים, and יום הכפורים does not do that job. So he must still bring it.
steps.whatToRemember: For both the מצורע and the נזיר, the קרבן is brought to permit eating קדשים, not for כפרה. So יום הכפורים does not replace it.

phrases.english: When a nazir brings an offering,
he does not bring it for atonement,
it is to become permitted to eat sacrificial food.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר כִּי קָא מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן, לָאו לְכַפָּרָה מַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 with the same reasoning as step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a נזיר is a חוטא, his קרבן is for כפרה and יום הכפורים covers it.
steps.terutzMaskana: His קרבן permits him to eat קדשים, so it is still required after יום הכפורים.

steps.title: What about a ספק סוטה after יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a ספק סוטה should not bring her offering after יום הכפורים, since only the מקום knows if she sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, an uncertain סוטה who had יום הכפורים pass over her should not bring her offering, because יום הכפורים atoned for her. This is a sin that only the מקום knows about!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same challenge on a third case, a סוטה, whose sin is uncertain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the מצורע and נזיר, a סוטה's case really is about a possible sin. So it seems to fit the rule that יום הכפורים clears a doubtful sin known only to the מקום. If so, her offering should no longer be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman suspected of being unfaithful, where it is unknown if she sinned

phrases.english: But if that is so, an uncertain sotah,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעָבַר עָלֶיהָ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לָא תַּיְיתֵי,
phrases.english: for whom Yom Kippur has passed, should not bring her offering,
since Yom Kippur atoned for her,

phrases.aramaic: דְּחֵטְא שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמָּקוֹם!
phrases.english: for it is a sin that only the Omnipresent knows about!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, סְפֵק סוֹטָה, שֶׁעָבַר עָלֶיהָ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נזיר is settled, the same challenge is applied to the סוטה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that יום הכפורים atones for a doubtful sin known only to the מקום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סוטה's possible sin is hidden and known only to the מקום, so she should be exempt from her offering after יום הכפורים.

steps.title: First answer: sins, not impurities
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא answers with the פסוק again: 'for all their sins', not for all their impurities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הושעיא said: 'For all their sins', and not for all their impurities.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי הושעיא gives his familiar answer. The סוטה's offering is connected to טומאה, which יום הכפורים does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same פסוק-based answer given for the יולדת, מצורע and נזיר. It fits the סוטה because the תורה describes her act with the language of becoming טמא. So her offering falls outside what יום הכפורים atones for.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya said:
"For all their sins" – and not for all their impurities.
phrases.notes: The תורה speaks of the סוטה as becoming impure, in במדבר 5:13.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא: ״לְכׇל חַטֹּאתָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים clears the סוטה's doubtful sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her case counts as טומאה, which יום הכפורים does not cover.

steps.title: Second answer: the other man knows
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that this is not a sin only the מקום knows about, because the בועל knows.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The man she was with knows about it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. He says the סוטה's sin is not really hidden from everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only covers a sin that no person knows about. If she sinned, the man she was with knows it. So her case does not fit the rule at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The man suspected of being with the סוטה

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not argue about what יום הכפורים covers. He argues that the sin is not one 'only the מקום knows', so the rule never applies.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The paramour knows about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בּוֹעֵל מַכִּיר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case does not fit the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוטה's sin is known only to the מקום.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person, the בועל, knows about it, so יום הכפורים's special atonement does not apply.

steps.title: Third answer: the סוטה's offering clarifies the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a סוטה brings her offering to find out whether there was a sin, not to atone for one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When a סוטה brings her offering, she brings it to clarify whether there was a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third answer. He says the purpose of the סוטה's offering is not כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her offering is part of the process that reveals whether she sinned. Since it is not for atonement, יום הכפורים cannot replace it. This is like the earlier answers about the מצורע and נזיר, where the קרבן also had a purpose other than כפרה.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers for the סוטה: (1) her case is טומאה, not sin; (2) the בועל knows, so it is not hidden; (3) her offering is to clarify the sin, not to atone for it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
When a sotah brings her offering –
it is to clarify the sin (that she brings it).
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some leave them out. The meaning is the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: סוֹטָה כִּי מֵתְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 20. It uses the same kind of reasoning as step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוטה's offering is for כפרה, so יום הכפורים covers it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her offering clarifies whether there was a sin, so she must still bring it after יום הכפורים.

steps.title: What about an עגלה ערופה after יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. An unsolved murder is a sin only the מקום knows about, so after יום הכפורים the עגלה ערופה should not be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, an עגלה ערופה that יום הכפורים passed over should not be brought, since only the מקום knows who sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same challenge pattern as before, now applied to עגלה ערופה. Nobody knows who did the murder, so maybe יום הכפורים already atoned for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עגלה ערופה is brought when a body is found and the killer is unknown. That looks exactly like 'a sin only the מקום knows about'. So if יום הכפורים atones for such sins, it should cancel the need for the עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so (introduces a challenge from what was just said)
The heifer whose neck is broken, brought for an unsolved murder

phrases.english: But if that is so,
a heifer whose neck is broken
that Yom Kippur passed over it [should not be brought]! etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the same challenge as before: this is a sin only the מקום knows about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה שֶׁעָבַר עָלֶיהָ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same challenge pattern used for סוטה, now applied to עגלה ערופה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that יום הכפורים atones for a sin only the מקום knows about.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unsolved murder is known only to the מקום, so יום הכפורים should make the עגלה ערופה unnecessary.

steps.title: The murderer himself knows
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that this is not a sin only the מקום knows about, because the killer knows what he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The killer knows.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the same kind of answer he gave for סוטה. Someone, the killer, does know about this sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about יום הכפורים covers only a sin no person knows about. Here the murderer knows, so the case falls outside that rule and the עגלה ערופה is still brought.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The murderer knows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הוֹרֵג מַכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 using the same reasoning אביי used in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: it is not a sin known only to the מקום.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unsolved murder is a sin only the מקום knows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The murderer knows, so יום הכפורים does not cover it.

steps.title: The land gets atonement only one way
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from a פסוק: atonement for spilled blood comes only through a specific way, not through יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says, 'And for the land there will be no atonement for the blood spilled in it, except through the blood of the one who spilled it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge about עגלה ערופה with a פסוק. The פסוק shows that murder needs its own special atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the land cannot get atonement for spilled blood except in a specific way. That means יום הכפורים cannot do the job, even when the killer is unknown. So the עגלה ערופה must still be brought after יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: And for the land there will be no atonement

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse says:
"And for the land there will be no atonement
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:33. The פסוק ends: 'except through the blood of the one who spilled it.'

phrases.english: for the blood that was spilled in it, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אָמַר קְרָא: וְלָאָרֶץ לֹא יְכוּפַּר לַדָּם אֲשֶׁר שֻׁפַּךְ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 24, based on a פסוק instead of logic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based exception: murder has its own required atonement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים covers any sin known only to the מקום, including an unsolved murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק limits atonement for spilled blood to a specific way, so יום הכפורים does not cover it.

steps.title: The atonement reaches back to יציאת מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers from the עגלה ערופה פסוק itself: its atonement covers even killings from long ago, so earlier יום הכפורים days did not take care of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The פסוק says, 'Atone for Your people ישראל, whom You redeemed.' This atonement is fit to atone even for those who left מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third answer to the עגלה ערופה challenge. He reads the words of the עגלה ערופה ceremony as covering even the generation that left מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many יום הכפורים days have passed since the people left מצרים. If the עגלה ערופה still atones all the way back to them, those days of יום הכפורים clearly did not wipe out this kind of sin. So יום הכפורים does not cancel the need for the עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Atone for Your people (said at the עגלה ערופה ceremony)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The verse says:
"Atone for Your people Israel, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:8. The פסוק continues: 'whom You redeemed,' meaning from מצרים.

phrases.english: this atonement is fit
to atone for those who left Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אָמַר קְרָא: כַּפֵּר לְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 24, using a different פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based: the עגלה ערופה atonement reaches back past many יום הכפורים days.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים already took care of an unsolved murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עגלה ערופה atones back to the generation of מצרים, which shows יום הכפורים never covered this sin.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers for עגלה ערופה: אביי says the killer knows. רבא says a פסוק limits atonement for blood. רב פפא says the atonement reaches back to יוצאי מצרים.

steps.title: Why bring a חטאת if the sin is discovered after יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if יום הכפורים atones for unknown sins, a person who finds out about his sin after יום הכפורים should not have to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said יום הכפורים atones for a sin only the מקום knows about, say that when the person finds out after יום הכפורים, he also does not bring a חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the rule against the regular חטאת. Before יום הכפורים, nobody knew about the sin, so maybe יום הכפורים already erased it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until the person found out, his sin was known only to the מקום, and יום הכפורים passed during that time. By the rule we just accepted, יום הכפורים should have atoned. If so, there would be nothing left for a חטאת to atone for once he learns of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have said (uses an accepted point to raise a new question)
Sin offering, brought for a known unintentional sin

phrases.english: Now that you have said:

phrases.aramaic: חֵטְא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמָּקוֹם
phrases.english: a sin that only the Omnipresent knows about
Yom Kippur atones for it,
say: when it becomes known to him
after Yom Kippur
he also should not bring a sin offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ: חֵטְא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמָּקוֹם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves עגלה ערופה and applies the same rule to a regular חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The obligation to bring a חטאת for a sin discovered after יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before discovery, the sin was known only to the מקום, so יום הכפורים should already have atoned for it.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a doubtful sin (אשם תלוי). The sin is certain, but the person only found out about it after יום הכפורים.

steps.title: The תורה writes 'knowing' three times
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירא answers that the תורה mentions 'knowing' for the individual's חטאת, the נשיא's, and the community's. This teaches that once a person knows, he brings a חטאת even after יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא said: You cannot say that, because the פסוק writes 'knowing' for a חטאת, for a נשיא, and for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זעירא rejects the idea that the חטאת is cancelled. He points out that the תורה uses the word for 'knowing' in three places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing 'knowing' three times looks like more than needed. רבי זעירא learns from it that knowledge of the sin always brings the חטאת obligation, whenever the knowing happens. So finding out after יום הכפורים still requires a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing, becoming aware of the sin
The leader or king, who brings his own type of חטאת

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא: לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: You cannot say this,
for the verse writes "knowing" regarding a sin offering,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:28. This is the חטאת of a regular person.

phrases.english: and regarding a Nasi, and regarding the community.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:23 and 4:14.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא: לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ, דִּכְתִיב קְרָא יְדִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based: the extra mentions of 'knowing' create the obligation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים atoned, so no חטאת is needed after discovering the sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whenever a person comes to know of his sin, he must bring a חטאת, even after יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Each mention of 'knowing' is needed on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבי זעירא. Each mention of 'knowing' is needed, because the נשיא and the community could not be learned from the individual, whose offering is always female.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are needed. If the פסוק had written it only by an individual, I would have said the others cannot be learned from the individual, since one can argue: an individual is different, because his offering is always female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זעירא's proof. It starts to show that none of the three mentions is extra, so they cannot teach his new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זעירא's proof depends on the three mentions being more than necessary. The גמרא says the individual's case is different, since his חטאת is a female animal while the נשיא brings a male goat and the community brings a bull. So the rule could not be copied from the individual to the others, and the תורה needed to write 'knowing' by them too.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed (each case teaches something the others cannot)
To refute, to point out a difference that breaks the comparison

phrases.english: They are needed,
for if the verse had written it regarding an individual,
I would have said:
all of them cannot be learned from an individual,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the נשיא and the community.

phrases.english: because one can refute:
what about an individual? He is different, since all his offering is female.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי כְּתַב קְרָא גַּבֵּי יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 29 by showing the three mentions of 'knowing' are not extra.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי זעירא's derivation, not the halacha itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the repeated word is extra. In fact each mention is needed, because the individual's female offering makes his case different from the others.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא here is not saying a person who finds out after יום הכפורים is exempt. It is only questioning רבי זעירא's source, and the argument continues past this point.

steps.title: Suggestion: write 'knowing' only by the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the תורה could have written 'knowing' only by the נשיא and learned the individual and the community from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה write it by the נשיא, and let us learn these other cases from the נשיא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new way the תורה could have saved words: mention 'knowing' only by the נשיא. This line sets up the next two steps, which knock the idea down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 showed we cannot learn the others from the individual. Now the גמרא asks whether the נשיא could be the one source case. If he could, two mentions would be extra, and רבי זעירא's teaching would come back.

keyTerms.meaning: The king or leader, who brings his own kind of חטאת
Let it write (let the תורה write)
And let us bring / learn it

phrases.english: Let it write it by the נשיא,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the word about 'knowing' of the sin.

phrases.english: and let us learn these from the נשיא!
phrases.notes: 'These' are the individual and the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְתּוֹב גַּבֵּי נָשִׂיא, וְנַיְיתֵי הָנָךְ מִנָּשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 30 ruled out the individual as the source case, this tries the נשיא as the source case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 30 that every mention of 'knowing' is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one mention by the נשיא could teach the other two cases, then two mentions are extra and could be used for רבי זעירא's teaching.

steps.title: The individual cannot be learned from the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא does not bring a קרבן for שמיעת קול, but the individual does. So the individual cannot be learned from the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The individual cannot be learned from the נשיא, because you can find a difference: the נשיא is not included in שמיעת קול. Can you say the same about the individual, who is included in שמיעת קול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning the individual from the נשיא, because there is a difference between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the נשיא is more lenient: he is never obligated in a קרבן for שמיעת קול. The individual is stricter, since he is obligated in it. Something lenient cannot teach about something stricter, so the individual needs its own mention.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute: we can point out a difference that blocks the learning
What about X? It is special because... (the form of a refutation)
Hearing a voice: the false oath that you know no testimony, which carries a קרבן

phrases.english: The individual cannot be learned from the נשיא,
because it can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְנָשִׂיא, שֶׁכֵּן אֵין בִּשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל,
phrases.english: What about the נשיא? He is special, because he is not included in 'hearing a voice,'
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 5:1, the oath about testimony. The king does not testify, so this קרבן does not apply to him.

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּיָחִיד שֶׁכֵּן יֶשְׁנוֹ בִּשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל!
phrases.english: can you say the same about the individual, who is included in 'hearing a voice'?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָחִיד מִנָּשִׂיא לָא אָתֵי, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first half of the suggestion in step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the individual from the נשיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The נשיא is lenient because he is not obligated in שמיעת קול, while the individual is.

steps.title: The community cannot be learned from the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא's קרבנות include a female animal, but the community's never do. So the community cannot be learned from the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The community cannot be learned from the נשיא, because you can find a difference: the נשיא is special, since among his קרבנות there is a female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second half of the suggestion: learning the community from the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of difference as in step 30. Any case whose קרבן can be female cannot teach about the community, whose קרבן is always male. So the community needs its own mention too, and the 'only by the נשיא' idea fails.

phrases.english: And the community cannot be learned from the נשיא,
because it can be refuted:
What about the נשיא? He is special, because among his offerings there is a female!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצִבּוּר מִנָּשִׂיא לָא אָתֵי, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes rejecting the suggestion in step 31, using the same kind of difference as step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the community from the נשיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The נשיא's offerings include a female, unlike the community's offerings, which are always male.

steps.title: Suggestion: write 'knowing' only by the community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the תורה could have written 'knowing' only by the community and learned the individual and the נשיא from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה write it by the community, and let us learn the individual and the נשיא from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option: the community as the one source case. This sets up the final rejection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The individual and the נשיא have both been ruled out as the source case. The only option left is the community. If this works, two mentions would still be extra.

phrases.english: Let it write it by the community,
and let us learn the individual and the נשיא from it!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְתּוֹב גַּבֵּי צִבּוּר, וְנַיְיתֵי יָחִיד וְנָשִׂיא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נשיא failed as the source case, this tries the community.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every mention of 'knowing' is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one mention by the community could teach the other two cases, the other mentions would be extra.

steps.title: The individual and the נשיא cannot be learned from the community
steps.stepSummary: The community is liable only for a court's mistaken ruling together with a mistaken action. So the individual and the נשיא cannot be learned from it, and all three mentions are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can find a difference: the community is special, because it is liable only for הֶעֱלֵם דָּבָר together with שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last option too. It points out that the community is liable only in a narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The community brings its חטאת only when the court ruled by mistake and the people then acted by mistake. That is a lenient rule, so it cannot teach about the individual and the נשיא. Since no case can teach the others, every mention of 'knowing' is needed. רבי זעירא's proof is still pushed away.

keyTerms.meaning: The court forgot or mistook a law and ruled wrongly
A mistaken action: the people acted on that wrong ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three cases (individual, נשיא, community) has something special, so none of them can be learned from just one other case. Learning one case from the other two together is tried next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the defense of step 30 against learning from a single case. Next the גמרא tries learning from two cases together, and in step 44 it finds a source for the step 28 question about a person who finds out after יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about the community?
It is special, because they are liable only

phrases.aramaic: עַל הֶעֱלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: for a mistaken ruling together with a mistaken action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְצִבּוּר, שֶׁכֵּן אֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל הֶעֱלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 34, finishing the defense of step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the individual and the נשיא from the community
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The community is liable only for a mistaken court ruling together with a mistaken action, which makes it more lenient.

steps.title: Learn the individual's 'knowing' from the other two
steps.stepSummary: Granted that one mention cannot teach the other two, the גמרא suggests learning one mention from two: skip 'knowing' by the יחיד and learn it from the נשיא and the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, two cannot be learned from one 'knowing'. But let one 'knowing' be learned from two: let the תורה not write 'knowing' by the individual, and learn it from the נשיא and the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits one mention cannot teach the other two, so it tries a new idea. Maybe one mention can be learned from the other two together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method has changed. Before, the גמרא tried learning from one source. Now it combines two sources, which is harder to knock down, because a refutation must find something the two sources share that the third lacks. The first test is to drop the individual's mention.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Knowing': the sinner later finds out about his sin, which is what triggers the קרבן
Let it come, meaning let it be derived

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with steps 31–35. There, each case was tested against one source. Here, each case is tested against two sources combined.

phrases.english: Granted, from one 'knowing' it cannot be derived;
let one 'knowing' be derived from two:
let [the תורה] not write 'knowing' by the individual,
and let it be derived from the נשיא and the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵחֲדָא יְדִיעָה לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא יְדִיעָה מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After single-source learning failed, the גמרא moves to learning from two sources combined.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word 'knowing' by the individual
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two other cases already say 'knowing', the individual could be learned from them, so the individual's mention looks extra.

steps.title: The individual is different: he brings a קרבן for שמיעת קול
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails. The נשיא and the צבור share a leniency, since neither brings a קרבן for שמיעת קול, while the יחיד does.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: the נשיא and the community are special because they are not included in שמיעת קול. Can you say the same about the individual, who is included in שמיעת קול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last suggestion. It finds something the נשיא and the community have in common that the individual does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources are more lenient, since neither is obligated for שמיעת קול. The individual is stricter, because he is obligated for it. You cannot learn a stricter case from more lenient ones, so the individual needs his own mention of 'knowing'.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute, meaning the comparison can be broken
Hearing a voice: the sin of falsely swearing you know no testimony, which requires a קרבן
Standard refutation formula: 'What about X, which is special... can you say the same about Y?'

phrases.english: There is room to refute:
What about the נשיא and the community?
They are special in that they are not included in 'hearing a voice'.
Will you say the same about the individual, who is included in 'hearing a voice'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְנָשִׂיא וְצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the step 36 suggestion to learn the individual from the נשיא and the community.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the individual's 'knowing' from the נשיא and the community
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share a leniency (no שמיעת קול) that the individual does not share.

steps.title: Learn the community's 'knowing' from the individual and the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests skipping 'knowing' by the צבור and learning it from the יחיד and the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the verse not write 'knowing' by the community, and learn it from the 'knowing' of the individual and the נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second combination. This time it drops the community's mention and learns it from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שמיעת קול objection does not apply here, because the two sources are not both exempt from it. The individual is obligated, so the sources do not share that leniency. The גמרא now needs to check whether any other difference exists.

keyTerms.meaning: The community, which brings a קרבן when the court rules wrongly

phrases.aramaic: לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא יְדִיעָה גַּבֵּי צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: Let the verse not write 'knowing' by the community,
and let it be derived from the 'knowing' of the individual and the נשיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא יְדִיעָה גַּבֵּי צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first combination failed, the גמרא tries the next one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word 'knowing' by the community
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The individual and the נשיא both say 'knowing', so the community could be learned from them.

steps.title: The community never brings a female animal
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails. The יחיד and the נשיא can bring a female animal, but the צבור never does.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: the individual and the נשיא are special because their offerings include a female animal. Can you say the same about the community, whose offerings never include a female?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second combination. It finds something the individual and the נשיא share that the community does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the individual and the נשיא have a case of a female offering, so they have something in common. The community never does, so it is different. Because of this difference, the community cannot be learned from them and needs its own mention.

phrases.english: There is room to refute:
What about the individual and the נשיא?
They are special in that their offerings include a female,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are part of the corrected wording, so read it as 'their offerings'.

phrases.english: will you say the same about the community,
whose offerings do not include a female?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְיָחִיד וְנָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the step 38 suggestion to learn the community from the individual and the נשיא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the community's 'knowing' from the individual and the נשיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share a feature (a female offering) that the community never has.

steps.title: Learn the נשיא's 'knowing' from the individual and the community
steps.stepSummary: The last combination: skip 'knowing' by the נשיא and learn it from the יחיד and the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה not write 'knowing' by the נשיא, and learn it from the 'knowing' of the individual and the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the third and final combination. This time it drops the נשיא's mention and learns it from the individual and the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This combination is harder to refute. The individual and the community do not obviously share a feature that the נשיא lacks, so the גמרא will now test each possible objection one by one.

phrases.english: Let [the תורה] not write ['knowing'] by the נשיא,
and let it be derived from the 'knowing' of the individual and the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב גַּבֵּי נָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the third and final combination after the first two failed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word 'knowing' by the נשיא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The individual and the community both say 'knowing', so the נשיא could be learned from them.

steps.title: The שמיעת קול objection fails: the individual proves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what refutation could block learning the נשיא from the other two. If it is that the צבור is exempt from שמיעת קול, the יחיד shows this does not matter, because he is obligated in it and still has 'knowing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you use to refute this? If you say it is because [the community] is not included in שמיעת קול, the individual proves otherwise, since his status regarding שמיעת קול is the opposite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now defends the suggestion by testing possible objections. It rejects the first one, שמיעת קול, using the individual as a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like a 'יוכיח' argument: the two sources differ on שמיעת קול, so that feature cannot be the reason they have 'knowing'. Since the community and the individual do not share a status here, שמיעת קול cannot stop the נשיא from being learned from them. The גמרא goes on to test other objections.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove: a counter-example that cancels a proposed difference

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גמרא is defending the suggestion, not attacking it. It shows that a possible objection does not work.

phrases.english: What refutation can you offer?
If it is because they are not included in 'hearing a voice',
phrases.notes: He means the community, which is not obligated for שמיעת קול.

phrases.english: the individual will prove [otherwise],
for [he is different] regarding 'hearing a voice',
phrases.notes: The point is that the individual is obligated for שמיעת קול, as step 37 said. So this difference cannot be what decides the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי פָּרְכַתְּ? אִי מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵינָן בִּשְׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל – יָחִיד יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the step 40 suggestion by rejecting the first possible refutation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible refutation that the community is exempt from שמיעת קול
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two sources do not share this feature, since the individual is obligated, so it cannot block the comparison.

steps.title: The female-offering difference does not block the learning either
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the יחיד is different because his offering is always a female. The צבור proves this does not matter: it never brings a female and still needs 'knowing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to block the learning because the יחיד always brings a female animal, the צבור proves otherwise. The צבור never brings a female, and it still needs 'knowing'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down a second possible objection to learning the נשיא from the יחיד and the צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could say the יחיד is a special case because all his sin offerings are female. But the צבור never brings a female, and it still has the rule of 'knowing'. So being female is not what creates the rule, and this objection fails too.

keyTerms.meaning: A female animal brought as an offering
Will prove: the other case shows the objection does not matter

phrases.english: And if it is because there is
a female in all of his sin offerings
phrases.notes: This is talking about the יחיד, whose sin offering is always a female goat or sheep.

phrases.english: the community will prove otherwise
for there is no female in their offerings

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִשּׁוּם דְּיֵשׁ בְּכׇל קׇרְבָּנוֹ נְקֵבָה צִבּוּר יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same back-and-forth (יוכיח) that began in step 41.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the possible objection based on female offerings.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The צבור has no female offering and still needs 'knowing', so being female is not the deciding factor.

steps.title: So why does the Torah write 'knowing' by the נשיא?
steps.stepSummary: Both the יחיד and the צבור need 'knowing' before they must bring an offering, so the נשיא could be learned from them. Then why is 'knowing' written by the נשיא at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them are not obligated until they have 'knowing'. So the נשיא would be the same. Why do I need the word 'knowing' written by the נשיא?
steps.whatsHappening: With both objections gone, the learning from the יחיד and the צבור works. So the גמרא asks why the תורה needed to write 'knowing' by the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What the יחיד and the צבור have in common is that neither is obligated before 'knowing', so the נשיא follows them. That makes the word in the נשיא's section look extra. An extra word in the תורה must be teaching something, so the גמרא asks what.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing: becoming aware of the sin, needed before one brings a חטאת
Why do I need it? A question pointing out an extra word
The ruler or king, who brings a male goat as his sin offering

phrases.english: until they have knowing
one is not obligated
why do I need what is written,
knowing by the נשיא?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי דִּכְתִיב יְדִיעָה גַּבֵּי נָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the now-successful learning to show the word by the נשיא is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'knowing' written in the נשיא's section
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it can be learned from the יחיד and the צבור, writing it again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The extra word teaches the case of finding out after יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: Since the word is not needed for the נשיא himself, we use it for another case: someone who finds out about his sin after יום הכפורים still brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the word is not needed for its own subject, since that is learned from the יחיד and the צבור, apply it to a different case. If he finds out about his sin after יום הכפורים, he brings a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the extra word teaches a new rule about sins discovered after יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that when a word is not needed where it is written, we use it to teach something else. Here it teaches that יום הכפורים does not cancel the חטאת. If the sin becomes known only after יום הכפורים, he still has to bring it.

keyTerms.term: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְגוּפֵיהּ תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן
keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own subject, apply it to another subject

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'knowing' by the נשיא teaches that a sin found out after יום הכפורים still requires a חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that יום הכפורים does not take away the obligation of a חטאת for a sin that becomes known only later.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for its own subject
since it is learned from the individual and the community
apply it to the subject
of where it becomes known to him
after יום הכפורים
that he brings a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְגוּפֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 43.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving an extra word to a new subject (אם אינו ענין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'knowing' by the נשיא seemed to have no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a sin found out after יום הכפורים still requires a חטאת.

steps.title: אביי: the נשיא could not have been learned from the others
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the learning from the יחיד and the צבור fails. Their offerings are fixed and do not change, which is not true of the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If 'knowing' were not written by the נשיא, we could not learn it from the יחיד and the צבור. That is because we can object: the יחיד and the צבור are special, since they are not likely to change. Will you say...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the whole learning from steps 40 to 44. He starts giving an objection that shows the נשיא is different, and his sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps said 'knowing' by the נשיא was extra because it could be learned from the יחיד and the צבור. אביי says that learning does not work, because the יחיד and the צבור share a feature the נשיא lacks: they are not apt to change. If he is right, the word by the נשיא is needed for itself and is not free to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute: to point out a difference that breaks a comparison

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing about the rule of 'knowing' itself. He agrees the נשיא needs 'knowing'. He only says it could not be learned from the others, so the תורה had to write it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא כְּתִיב יְדִיעָה גַּבֵּי נָשִׂיא,
phrases.english: If knowing were not written by the נשיא
it could not be learned from the individual and the community
because there is room to refute it:
What about the individual and the community?
They are not apt to change
Will you say
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here. It continues on the next amud, talking about the נשיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר אִי דְּלָא כְּתִיב יְדִיעָה גַּבֵּי נָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in steps 43 and 44 that the word by the נשיא is extra.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the נשיא from the יחיד and the צבור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The יחיד and the צבור are not apt to change, a feature the נשיא does not share.
